title: Promising disruptors of p53-MDM2 dimerization from some medicinal plant phytochemicals: a molecular modeling study.
authors: Oyedele, Abdul-Quddus Kehinde; Adelusi, Temitope Isaac; Ogunlana, Abdeen Tunde; Ayoola, Mojeed Ashiru; Adeyemi, Rofiat Oluwabusola; Babalola, Musa Oladayo; Ayorinde, James Babatunde; Isong, Josiah Ayoola; Ajasa, Toheeb Olakunle; Boyenle, Ibrahim Damilare
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过分子对接和MD模拟筛选植物化合物抑制p53-MDM2蛋白-蛋白互作，对象为蛋白-蛋白而非蛋白-DNA互作，方法虽含物理模拟但与本课题TF-DNA结合机制无关。
abstract: Cancer is a major global health issue that has a high mortality rate. p53, which functions as a tumor suppressor, is critical in preventing tumor development by regulating the cell cycle and inducing apoptosis in damaged cells. However, the tumor suppressor function of p53 is effectively inhibited by its direct interaction with the hydrophobic cleft of MDM2 protein via multiple mechanisms As a result, restoring p53 activity by blocking the p53-MDM2 protein-protein interaction has been proposed as a compelling therapeutic strategy for cancer treatment. The use of molecular docking and phytochemical screening procedures are appraised to inhibit MDM2's hydrophobic cleft and disrupt the p53-MDM2 interaction. For this purpose, a library of 51 bioactive compounds from 10 medicinal plants was compiled and subjected to structure-based virtual screening. Out of these, only 3 compounds (Atalantoflavone, Cudraxanthone 1, and Ursolic acid) emerged as promising inhibitors of MDM2-p53 based on their binding affinities (-9.1 kcal/mol, -8.8 kcal/mol, and -8.8 kcal/mol respectively) when compared to the standard (-8.8 kcal/mol). Moreover, these compounds showed better pharmacokinetic and drug-like profiling than the standard inhibitor (Chromonotriazolopyrimidine 1). Finally, the 100 ns MD simulation analysis confirmed no significant perturbation in the conformational dynamics of the simulated binary complexes when compared to the standard. In particular, Ursolic acid was found to satisfy the molecular enumeration the most compared to the other inhibitors. Our overall molecular modeling finding shows why these compounds may emerge as potent arsenals for cancer therapeutics. Nonetheless, extensive experimental and clinical research is needed to augment their use in clinics.Communicated by Ramaswamy H. Sarma.
abstract_zh: 癌症是一个具有高死亡率的重大全球健康问题。p53作为肿瘤抑制因子，通过调控细胞周期和诱导受损细胞凋亡，在阻止肿瘤发展中起关键作用。然而，p53的肿瘤抑制功能因其与MDM2蛋白的疏水裂缝直接相互作用而通过多种机制被有效抑制。因此，通过阻断p53-MDM2蛋白-蛋白相互作用来恢复p53活性，已被提出作为癌症治疗的一种有前景的策略。采用分子对接 (molecular docking) 和植物化学筛选程序来抑制MDM2的疏水裂缝并破坏p53-MDM2相互作用。为此，从10种药用植物中汇编了51种生物活性化合物的库，并进行基于结构的虚拟筛选。其中，仅有3种化合物（Atalantoflavone、Cudraxanthone 1和Ursolic acid）因其结合亲和力（分别为-9.1 kcal/mol、-8.8 kcal/mol和-8.8 kcal/mol）与标准物（-8.8 kcal/mol）相比，而成为MDM2-p53的有前景抑制剂。此外，这些化合物显示出比标准抑制剂（Chromonotriazolopyrimidine 1）更好的药代动力学和类药特性。最后，100 ns的分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟分析确认，与标准物相比，模拟的二元复合物在构象动力学上没有显著扰动。特别是，Ursolic acid被发现最符合分子枚举要求，优于其他抑制剂。我们的整体分子建模发现解释了这些化合物为何可能成为癌症治疗的有力武器。尽管如此，仍需广泛的实验和临床研究以增强其在临床中的应用。由Ramaswamy H. Sarma通讯。
